title: Orunmila verdict record, schema version 1: DRAFT
description: One verdict on one sealed odù record: Clean, Look at this or Violation, with its receipt. A line of the verdict log, hash-chained like the other two logs. Same odù records plus same rules always give the same verdicts, so a verdict holds no clock.
$comment: brief v4 lines 642-686; guarantees 3, 4, 6, 8 (lines 490-495); Q34, approved by O 2026-11-24 (LD262). Unknown fields are allowed (brief v4 line 209).

record.description: Marks this line as a verdict on one odù.
record.$comment: agent's choice, as the odù log's records (LD167)

seq.description: The record's place in the verdict log: the header is 0, records follow from 1.

verdict_id.description: The verdict's id, unique in its log; a later verdict names an earlier one by it in `supersedes`.

odu_hash.description: That odù's hash in the odù log, so the verdict points at exactly one record.
odu_hash.$comment: brief v4 line 684 (points back to the odù it judged); agent's choice of field, Q34

verdict.description: Three verdicts, nothing else: clean, look_at_this, violation.

rule.description: The rule that decided the verdict, by its id in the rule set (R0: no rule found anything, so the odù is Clean). For a parent raised by a child, the child's rule.
rule.$comment: brief v4 line 659 (the rule that fired)

also.description: Every other rule that fired on the odù, by id, sorted; empty when none did.
also.$comment: agent's choice, Q34: line 659 cites one rule, and an odù can break more than one

mark_seqs.description: The receipt: the odù's marks. A verdict without a receipt cannot exist.

witness_status.description: The odù's witness_status, copied, so the verdict log alone shows what each witness recorded.

hidden.description: True when the default view hides the odù: a Clean reverted change, or a Clean mark that changes nothing on disk.

opened.description: For a parent: the children whose own verdict is more serious than the parent's own and raised it; empty otherwise.

supersedes.description: null, or the earlier verdict on the same odù that a re-judgement replaces. Old verdicts are never edited.

rules.description: The fingerprint of the rule set that judged it: SHA-256 of the rules file's bytes.
